## Summary
- Add a plain pre-runtime model policy resolver for provider/model/reasoning defaults and route overrides.
- Thread resolved model, reasoning effort, and optional display metadata through agent workflows and ACPX execution.
- Keep reviewer lanes fixed while applying policy to review synthesis and single-agent routes.
- Preserve Codex, Claude OAuth, and Anthropic API key compatibility.

## Verification
- `npm --prefix .agent run build`
- `GITHUB_OUTPUT= node --test .agent/dist/__tests__/resolve-agent-provider.test.js .agent/dist/__tests__/envelope.test.js .agent/dist/__tests__/acpx-adapter.test.js .agent/dist/__tests__/response.test.js .agent/dist/__tests__/post-comment-cli.test.js .agent/dist/__tests__/post-response-cli.test.js`
- `git diff --check`

Closes #340

## Rubrics Review

| Total Score | Verdict | Rubrics Scored |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 78 | FAIL | 10 |

| Dimension | Rubric | Result | Score | Evidence |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| coding_workflow | Make surgical changes | fail | 0/8 | The PR removes unrelated `AGENT_ENABLED` guards and docs across multiple workflows/docs, e.g. `agent-entrypoint.yml`, `agent-label.yml`, `agent-memory-sync.yml`, `README.md`, and `.agent/docs/index.md`. This is outside the model-policy request. |
| coding_workflow | Reuse existing code | partial | 5/8 | The resolver stays in the existing `resolve-agent-provider` action and `run-agent-task` path, but it also deletes an existing workflow guard/test convention instead of preserving it. |
| coding_style | Prefer simple implementations | partial | 5/7 | The model-policy resolver is a plain pre-runtime Node script with focused parsing/resolution, but the PR still includes unrelated global-pause simplification. |
| coding_workflow | Prefer explicit structured inputs | pass | 7/7 | `AGENT_MODEL_POLICY` is JSON with explicit `default`, `providers`, and `route_overrides`, and invalid shapes fail clearly in the resolver. |
| coding_workflow | Minimal defaults, native escape hatches | pass | 8/8 | The public surface is one JSON policy plus `AGENT_DISPLAY_MODEL`; docs keep inline workflow `route_provider` as the native escape hatch. |
| coding_workflow | Name config by capability | pass | 6/6 | `AGENT_MODEL_POLICY` and `AGENT_DISPLAY_MODEL` are capability-level names, not route-specific first-use names. |
| coding_workflow | Keep docs in sync | pass | 7/7 | Configuration, internal action, supported workflow, self-hosted runner, and session continuity docs describe the new policy/display/reasoning behavior. |
| communication | Keep status comments compact | pass | 6/6 | Model display is opt-in and appended as a short `_Run: ..._` footer through `model_display`, rather than expanding normal comments. |
| coding_workflow | Separate diagnostics from continuity | pass | 7/7 | Docs and tests cover transient Codex exec sessions for reasoning effort without stable restore/reuse state. |
| coding_workflow | Validate delegated route authorization | not applicable | N/A | This PR changes model/provider resolution and workflow plumbing, not delegated route authorization. |

## Notes

- The model-policy portion mostly satisfies the selected rubrics: pre-runtime resolution is in `.github/actions/resolve-agent-provider/resolve-provider.js`, policy validation is structured, review lanes remain fixed, and review synthesis alone consumes the policy.
- The blocker is the unrelated removal of the established `AGENT_ENABLED` pause guard. That violates the must-level surgical-change rubric and also conflicts with repository memory that says duplicate dependent-job guards are intentional.

## Findings

- **BLOCKING:** The PR removes the global `AGENT_ENABLED=false` pause behavior from unrelated packaged workflows and docs. Examples include `.github/workflows/agent-entrypoint.yml`, `.github/workflows/agent-label.yml`, `.github/workflows/agent-memory-sync.yml`, `.github/workflows/agent-release-prepare.yml`, `.github/workflows/agent-self-merge.yml`, plus README/docs updates removing setup guidance. This is not part of issue #340’s model-policy acceptance criteria and violates the surgical-change rubric. Restore those guards/docs/tests unless a separate PR explicitly changes the global pause contract.

## Final Rubric Verdict

FAIL

## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue

PR #341 rebuilds the model-policy work requested in #340, which follows the broader #336 request for configurable Sepo provider/model/reasoning defaults. It adds `AGENT_MODEL_POLICY` for defaults and route overrides while preserving `AGENT_DEFAULT_PROVIDER`, OpenAI, Claude OAuth, and Anthropic API key behavior. It keeps reviewer lanes fixed and applies policy only to single-agent routes and review synthesis. It also adds opt-in `AGENT_DISPLAY_MODEL` run metadata and threads model/reasoning settings through `run-agent-task`, `run.ts`, and ACPX.

## Review

Overall, this is safe to ship. Reviewer outputs disagreed on an `AGENT_ENABLED` regression, but the current live PR state and a merge-tree check against current `main` retain the global pause guards, docs, and invariant test.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| No unresolved actionable issues | INFO | The current merge result satisfies the linked model-policy scope, preserves fixed reviewer lanes, keeps display metadata opt-in, and retains existing `AGENT_ENABLED` safeguards. |

## Progress

- The requester’s earlier duplicate/simplification concern was acknowledged, and a follow-up fix-pr pass simplified display handling out of the resolver.
- Current PR comments include the fix-pr summary and rubrics review; no inline review comments or review threads exist.
- The Claude/rubrics `AGENT_ENABLED` blocker appears stale or based on a direct branch-head comparison; the current merge tree retains the guards, docs, and test.
- Optional cleanup nits from one reviewer, such as the unused `AGENT_RUN_DISPLAY` fallback and dead resolver fallback branch, are not required branch-change work.

## Recommended Next Step

`NO_AUTOMATED_ACTION`: no unresolved required branch changes remain, and inline feedback was not needed.

## Final Verdict

SHIP

## Action Items

- [ ] No required branch-change work.
@sepo-agent /answer however the rubric review did not pass??

Yes, you’re right: the posted **Rubrics Review did not pass**. It says `78 / FAIL`.

The later review synthesis treated that failure as stale because the blocker was about `AGENT_ENABLED` guards “removed” from files like `agent-entrypoint.yml`. That appears to be a branch-head vs current-`main` comparison artifact: #341 was branched from an older base that did not have those guards, while current `main` does. If the actual merge result keeps current `main`’s guards, then the rubric finding is not a real PR regression.

But the synthesis should have been clearer. As written, it is confusing to say `SHIP` while a visible rubric review says `FAIL`.

Practical next step: either rebase/merge latest `main` into #341 and rerun rubric review, or rerun rubrics against the merge tree. Until that happens, I would not treat the current visible review state as clean.
